decisions.context: Authorization needs a synchronous score within tens of milliseconds. The model must fit a request path that can keep serving through peak load.
decisions.rationale: Choose a separately deployable model service to scale the scoring tier for peaks; validate the added network hop against the latency budget. (d:1, v:1.1)
consequences: Operate model service availability and capacity.

decisions.context: Each transaction needs a score before authorization proceeds, so predictions must be available online. Serving capacity must handle peaks.
decisions.rationale: Choose real-time microservice serving to scale scoring independently during peaks; verify the network path meets the tens-of-milliseconds constraint. (d:5, v:5.1)
consequences: Provide capacity headroom and service health checks.
Keep request and model loading overhead within the latency budget.

decisions.context: The scoring path needs features for each transaction, and the audit record must identify which features produced each score. The brief does not specify feature freshness or access patterns.

alternatives.label: Store features in data stores without specific support

decisions.rationale: Choose a feature store as a dedicated place to retrieve scoring features and support feature traceability. The design space does not establish that it meets the service latency budget, so confirm that in implementation. (d:4, v:4.1)
consequences: Record feature identities or snapshots with each score.
Feature lookup latency becomes part of the request budget.

decisions.context: Auditors need the model version associated with every score. Rollout and rollback should preserve the ability to identify which version handled a transaction.
decisions.rationale: Choose rollback to a prior version to provide a recovery path while logging the active model version for each score. The local design point had no warnings but no attesting sources; this is a novel, unchecked-in-practice combination in this design space. (d:10, v:10.2)
consequences: Retain deployable model artifacts and version metadata.
Log model version with every score.

decisions.context: Auditors need to reconstruct which model and features produced a score. The scoring service also needs operational visibility while handling transaction peaks.

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
Model performance monitoring
cons: Does not alone identify each score

decisions.rationale: Choose tracking that includes inputs and outputs so score records can be associated with their model and features; apply retention and access controls appropriate to transaction data. (d:22, v:22.4)
consequences: Persist model version and feature references with score records.
Tracking adds storage and processing load.

decisions.context: The score is on the authorization path and must meet a tight response time at peak load. Failures or slowdowns could delay transaction authorization.
decisions.rationale: Choose performance testing because the brief sets a response-time constraint and peak availability requirement; API and integration checks remain useful complementary coverage. (d:26, v:26.13)
consequences: Use representative transaction and peak-load profiles.
Retest latency when model or feature access changes.

uncovered: Exact latency objective and peak transaction rate.
Feature definitions, freshness, storage layout, and retention policy.
Audit record schema, retention period, access controls, and privacy requirements.
Model training, validation, approval, and release criteria.
Availability targets, failover behavior, and authorization behavior when scoring is unavailable.
Runtime, deployment platform, and service communication protocol.
